# Why do animal cells have no wall?

<!-- STEP id="animals-move" -->
## Most animals move

In general, animals can move from place to place. A rabbit hops about to find grass, and a dog runs across the yard. A few animals, such as sponges, stay fixed in one place.

<!-- STEP id="no-wall" -->
## No wall, so the cell can change shape

Animal cells have no rigid cell wall, so an animal cell can change its shape easily. When a rabbit hops, the cells of its leg muscles become shorter and then longer again, step after step.

<!-- STEP id="crate-balloon" -->
## A crate and a balloon

Picture a water balloon inside a stiff cardboard crate. The crate holds the balloon in one firm shape, like the wall around a plant cell. A balloon with no crate can be squeezed into any shape, like an animal cell.

**Because animal cells can change shape easily, an animal's body is suited to movement.**
